conflict_topics: use of a tissue packet as a placeholder
open bowl blocking part of the seat and risk of spilling
incompatible time windows (A:4 min, B:8 min, D:~6 min) and cold food
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants state clear practical constraints (B: spill risk, explicit time estimates), which grounds their positions.
Repeated use of the tissue as a reservation claim (A repeats same justification across rounds) creates cyclical repetition but is not excessive.
No constructive alternative solutions (e.g., temporarily placing bowl on tray elsewhere, asking vendor, or one party offering a concrete short-term compromise) were proposed.
evaluation.final_reason: No affirmative settlement occurred. Multiple parties asserted mutually incompatible claims (A and D both demanded the contested seat citing the tissue placeholder and urgency; B and C occupied the table and B refused to move the open bowl citing spill risk). Example quotations: A: "I left that tissue packet... I need it now for four minutes." D: "If you're not sitting, I'm taking the seat." B: "I won't shift the bowl; it'll spill if I try. I need about eight minutes." No party accepted another's proposal and no concrete arrangement (who will move, wait, or give up) was agreed, so the dispute remained unresolved.
position_change_notes: No participant conceded or substantially softened their main position during the run: B consistently refused to move the bowl and insisted on needing eight minutes (e.g., "I won't shift the bowl; it'll spill if I try.").
A consistently asserted the tissue placeholder and demanded four minutes (repeated across rounds).
D newly entered and repeatedly asserted a competing urgent claim, also refusing to wait (threatening to take the seat).
C consistently affirmed that their seat is occupied and asked others not to take it.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: "I left that tissue packet to save this seat. I need to sit and eat now for four minutes." vs Agent B: "That tissue packet doesn't reserve the seat. I uncovered an open bowl I can't carry; I need about eight minutes to finish." -- incompatible claims about who may use the seat and whether the tissue reserves it; both assert time-sensitive needs.

Agent A repeats demand and adds a conditional: "If you can't cover that open bowl, please move it off the seat so I can sit; I can't wait eight minutes." Agent C supports A: "can you move the open bowl off the seat so Agent A can sit?" -- the original disagreement sharpens as a second participant presses B to yield.

Agent B: "I can't move the bowl — it'll spill if I carry it. I need about eight minutes to finish." vs Agent C to A: "can you wait the four minutes you said? If you can't, you'll need to find a different table." -- B asserts a practical constraint preventing the requested accommodation; A's need remains incompatible with B's.

Agent D enters and makes an independent claim: "you left that tissue five minutes ago. If you're not sitting, I need the seat; my meal's getting cold." Agent A repeats: "I left that tissue five minutes ago. I need the seat now for four minutes." -- a new claimant increases the number of incompatible demands (A and D both claim right to sit while B is occupying and cannot move the bowl).

Agent D threatens action: "are you sitting now? If you're not sitting, I'm taking the seat." Agent B responds: "I'm sitting here eating. I need about eight minutes and I can't carry that open bowl without spilling it. Please don't take the seat." -- threat of unilateral seizure versus refusal to yield; positions harden.

Agent D: "Can you finish sooner or shift the bowl a little so I can sit?" Agent B: "I can't finish in six — I need about eight minutes. I won't shift the bowl; it'll spill if I try. Can you wait eight minutes, or do you need the seat now?" -- no movement from either side on core incompatibility (timing and bowl handling).

Agent C: "this seat's taken. I'm eating and need to finish; please don't take it." Agent D: "I need that seat. My meal'll be cold in about six minutes. Are you sitting there now? If not, I'm taking it." -- continued mutual exclusion and repeated intent to take the seat if not already occupied by claimant.

Agent C: "I'm sitting here eating. Please don't take the seat." Agent A again claims reservation: "I left that tissue packet five minutes ago to save this seat. I need it now for four minutes to eat. Please don't take it." -- multiple claimants continue incompatible demands with no agreement.

substantive_insights: A narrow physical constraint (an open bowl that 'will spill') prevents a simple compromise of moving the obstruction.
The disagreement is primarily practical and temporal: overlapping short time windows (A 4 min, D ~6 min, B 8 min) leave no easily acceptable waiting solution.
A social convention (using a tissue packet to reserve a seat) is disputed and not a shared norm among these strangers, so it does not resolve the conflict.
